sections.h2: What Gainesville interiors ask of a paint job
body: Indoor humidity in North Central Florida is not just a bathroom issue. Closets on exterior walls, laundry rooms, and kitchens all see condensation and steam, and flat builder paint in a hallway shows every handprint. Older homes in Duckpond and Pleasant Street add another layer: surfaces that have been repainted many times, sometimes over a glossy oil coat that new latex will not grip without sanding and a bonding primer.

In NW Gainesville bungalows we often find small cracks at corners and seams, and in newer Haile Plantation and Kanapaha-area homes the usual complaint is tired, scuffed flat paint that cannot be cleaned.

bullets: Patch nail pops, dings, and settlement cracks; feather and sand smooth
Spot-prime every repair so patches do not flash through the finish
Degloss and prime old enamel trim before switching systems
Caulk gaps at baseboards, casings, and crown
Treat any mildew in baths and closets at the source before painting

body: Sheen is where most interior repaints go wrong. A higher sheen cleans better but reveals wall flaws; a flatter one hides flaws but marks more easily. We usually suggest a washable matte or eggshell for living areas, satin in kitchens, baths, and kids' rooms, and waterborne urethane enamel on doors and trim for a hard, cleanable edge. Our guide to picking a paint finish for every room walks through the trade-offs.
Ceilings get a flat, non-reflective finish to hide roller laps. If your ceilings are still textured, popcorn ceiling removal can be added before the walls are painted.

Crews move and cover furniture, mask floors, and finish one room before opening the next, so you keep a working kitchen and a place to sleep. Low-VOC and eco-conscious products are available. A single room usually takes one day; a whole-home interior runs three days to two weeks depending on size, ceiling height, and the amount of repair.

A crew lead measures each room, notes repairs and sheen changes, and sends an itemized estimate, usually within one business day. Interior work can be scheduled any month, which makes it a good summer project while exteriors wait for drier weather. Our main interior painting page covers products in more detail. See how interior jobs fit into the rest of our Gainesville home painting work, or read about why drywall paint bubbles if you are seeing blisters already.

faqs.q: Do I need to empty the room before you arrive?
faqs.a: No. Clearing small breakables and wall hangings helps, but our crews move and protect furniture themselves and put it back when the room is done.

faqs.q: Can you paint over the glossy trim in my older Gainesville home?
faqs.a: Yes, after it is deglossed and primed with a bonding primer. Skipping that step is a common reason new trim paint peels.
We can match from a paint chip, a cabinet door, or a leftover can, and we show full-size drawdowns before committing.

faqs.q: Will my house smell like paint for days?
faqs.a: Low-VOC options keep odor to a minimum, and most rooms can be used again the same day they are finished.
